rule: docs/MRI_M0M1_PROTOCOL.md section 4: for each flagged study (label-blind image (b), no lesion outlines) decide keep Bosma22b / use Guerbet23 / exclude
decided_by: Claude (agent), 2026-11-10, on label-blind images; for the lead's review

10017_1000017.reason: both gland masks agree and outline the prostate at apex, mid and base; only the two zone models disagree (HeviAI23 vs Yuan23), which the protocol already handles: cells where the models disagree are 'zone uncertain'

11076_1001098.reason: gland masks agree at apex and mid-gland, small difference at the base; zone models disagree (Yuan23 PZ extends outside the gland), handled as 'zone uncertain'

11106_1001129.reason: mid-gland agrees; Bosma22b is a little wider at the apex and Guerbet23 covers more of a median-lobe protrusion at the base; Bosma22b (primary) is acceptable

11050_1001070.trigger: named as a faulty AI segmentation in the picai_labels README (known before M0); also surfaced by the M0 count of positives with an empty lesion crop
11050_1001070.reason: label-blind wide-field view (T2W + Bosma22b outline only, 256 mm field): the gland mask lies on anterior pelvic tissue, not on the prostate, and is fragmented in the sagittal view; Guerbet23 agrees with it (gland Dice 0.87), so neither AI gland mask is usable

extra_screen.rule: added after M0 ran (deviation, label-blind): AI gland volume (Bosma22b) / reported prostate_volume outside 0.5-2.0 -> label-blind visual check. Reason: agreement of two AI masks cannot catch a case where both are wrong (11050_1001070).
extra_screen.result: 754 studies, 739 with a reported volume; ratio median 0.93 (1st-99th pct 0.56-1.64); 2 outside 0.5-2.0; 11050_1001070 has ratio 1.80, so this screen would not have caught it

10541_1000552.reason: mask on the prostate at apex, mid, base, sagittal and coronal; the reported volume looks too small

11051_1001071.reason: mask on the prostate in all views; reported 4 ml is implausible (likely a clinical-sheet error). Note for M3: PSAD = PSA / reported volume would be inflated for this study
